Rashi on Chullin 7a:10:1.english: Ginai - The name of the river.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:11:1.english: The will of my Creator - All the rivers flow to the sea by the decree of the King [of the World].

Rashi on Chullin 7a:11:2.hebrew: ספק עושה - שמא לא יתנו לך בפדיון:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:11:2.english: Perhaps he makes - [I.e.,] perhaps they will not give it to you in redemption.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:12:1.hebrew: דבמצוה עסיק - דכתיב (שמות יב) "ושמרתם את המצות", דמתחלת טחינה והרקדה בעיא שימור לשם מצה:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:12:1.english: He is engaged in a mitzva - As it is written (Exodus 12): "And you shall guard the matzot," [which teaches] that from the start of the grinding and sifting, it requires guarding for the sake of matzah.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:12:2.english: Who joined them - He joined together with them on the road.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:12:4.english: Do they do so - [Said] with incredulity.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:12:5.hebrew: לבני לויה - לבני חבורה שמניחן והולך:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:12:5.english: For his companions - For his group, whom he leaves behind and goes on.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:13:1.hebrew: דלמא ה"נ חדא זימנא - אלא מתיירא היה שלא יחזרו המים וישטפו השנים, והיה מדבר עליהם שימתין להם הנהר:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:13:1.english: Perhaps here too it was one time - Rather, he [Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya'ir] was afraid that the water would return and sweep away the other two [who had not yet crossed], so he spoke to it concerning them, [instructing] that the river should wait for them.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:13:2.english: Like Moses and sixty myriads - For whom the Red Sea split.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:1:1.hebrew: מקום הניחו - כשיבאו בנינו אחרינו, אם לא ימצאו מה לתקן, במה יגדל שמם:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:1:1.english: A place they left - When our children come after us, if they do not find anything to improve, how will their name become great?

Rashi on Chullin 7a:1:2.english: To aggrandize himself - [This] means to make himself great.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:2:1.hebrew: מכאן - שראינו שקבל רבי עדות זו ולמד הימנה, אע"פ שדבר תימה הוא, שהרי מעולם היו נוהגין בו איסור, למדנו שאין מזיחין תלמיד חכם האומר דבר הלכה חידוש לאמר לא שמעת. אין מזיחין - אין מבדילין אותו משמועתו לאמר חזור בך:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:2:1.english: From here - Since we see that Rabbi accepted this testimony and derived a ruling from it, even though it is a surprising matter — for they had always treated it as forbidden — we learn that one does not rebuff a Torah scholar who states a halachic ruling as a novel teaching, by telling him, "You did not hear that." "One does not rebuff" - [This means] one does not turn him away from his tradition by telling him, "Retract."

Rashi on Chullin 7a:2:2.english: They reject [his words] - They treat his words with contempt.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:3:1.hebrew: זחוחי - לשון גבוהי הלב, שלא דקדק מפי רבו כל צרכו וסמכו על לבם:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:3:1.english: Haughty - An expression meaning "proud of heart" - [one] who did not learn with sufficient precision from his teacher and relied on his own judgment.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:4:1.english: He did not drive [them] out, etc. - Rather, they left them as tributary laborers, dwelling among them.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:5:1.english: It escaped him - [Meaning:] It escaped Yehuda the son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:5:2.hebrew: הרבה כרכים כבשו עולי מצרים - וקדשום בקדושת הארץ, ולא כבשום עולי בבל לקדשם בשניה, ולכך לא כבשום דקסברי הואיל והותרו הותרו, דקדושה ראשונה בטלה, דכי קדשה יהושע לשעתה קדשה ולא לעתיד לבא. כשגלו בימי נבוכדנצר ולא רצו להחזיר קדושתה, כדי שיהא מותר לחרוש ולזרוע שם בשביעית שאין נוהגת בחוצה לארץ, ויסמכו עליהן עניים ליטול לקט שכחה ופאה ומעשר עני, ובית שאן מהן היתה. ואותן שקדשו - הן לא בטלו בחורבן שני, כדאמרינן ביבמות בהערל (יבמות דף פב:): "והביאך ה' אלהיך אל הארץ אשר ירשו אבותיך וירשתה" - ירושה ראשונה ושניה יש להם, שבטלה ירושה ראשונה ונקראת שניה ירושה, אבל ירושה שלישית אין להם, שהשניה לא פסקה. הלכך בימי רבי נהגו איסור בארץ:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:5:2.english: Many cities did those who ascended from Egypt conquer - and they sanctified them with the sanctity of the Land, but those who ascended from Babylonia did not conquer them so as to sanctify them a second time. And the reason they did not conquer them is that they reasoned: since [these lands] were released [from the Land's sanctity], they remained released - for the first sanctification had lapsed, since when Joshua sanctified [the Land], he sanctified it only for his own time, and not for the future to come. When they were exiled in the days of Nebuchadnezzar [the first sanctification lapsed], and [the returnees from Babylonia] did not want to restore its sanctity, so that it would be permitted to plow and sow there during the Sabbatical year - since [the Sabbatical year] does not apply outside the Land - and so that the poor could rely on them to take the gleanings, the forgotten sheaf, the corner of the field, and the tithe for the poor. And Beit Shean was one of these [cities]. But those [cities] that they did sanctify - their [sanctity] was not annulled by the destruction of the Second [Temple], as we say in Yevamot, in [the chapter] HaArel (Yevamot 82b): "And the Lord your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it" - they have a first possession and a second possession, meaning that the first possession was annulled and [that land] is called by the second possession, but a third possession they do not have, for the second one never ceased. Therefore, in the days of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], they observed the [Sabbatical-year] prohibition in that land.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:7:1.hebrew: עלה בעלמא - דאכילת עראי היא, ושריא בארץ:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:7:1.english: An ordinary leaf - Since it is [a case of] incidental eating, it is permitted in the Land [of Israel].

Rashi on Chullin 7a:7:2.english: He ate it from a bundle - For once it is bound into a bundle, it is forbidden to eat from it casually [without tithing].

Rashi on Chullin 7a:7:3.english: That which is normally bound - Meaning, it is its practice to be bound.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:7:4.english: From when it is bound [into a sheaf] - It becomes fixed for tithing and is forbidden to be eaten casually.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:8:1.english: It was not on his mind - Rabbi Meir forgot and did not tithe them, but in principle he holds that they require tithing.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:9:1.hebrew: ממקום אחר - שמא הוי ליה ירק תלוש בביתו, ואמר: הרי הוא מעשר על אגודה זו:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:9:1.english: From another place - Perhaps he had cut vegetables at home, and he said: "This is tithe for this bundle."

Rashi on Chullin 7a:9:2.hebrew: לתרום שלא מן המוקף - מן המחובר וסמוך לו, כגון אין מקיפין שתי חביות (ביצה דף לב:), וכמו מקפת וקורא לה שם (נדה דף עא:), לשון מקריב ומגיען זה לזה. ואסור לחבר להפריש ממה שאין לפניו על מה שלפניו, דשמא אותו שהוא סומך עליו אינו בעין שנאבד או נרקב, ונמצא שאין אומר כלום ואוכל טבלים:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:9:2.english: To tithe from produce not adjoining [the rest] - [Meaning] from that which is attached and close to it, similar to "one does not encircle two barrels [together]" (Beitzah 32b), and like "she encircles it and gives it a name" (Niddah 71b) - a term denoting bringing near, so that they reach one another. And a chaver is forbidden to separate [terumah] from produce that is not before him on behalf of that which is before him, for perhaps the produce he is relying on is no longer there, having been lost or rotted, in which case his declaration means nothing, and he ends up eating untithed produce.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:9:3.english: He set his eyes on this side - To designate it as the tithe for the other side, and he ate from the other side.

Rashi on Chullin 7a:9:4.hebrew: חזי מאן גברא רבה אסהיד עליה - ראה כמה אדם גדול העיד עליו, דהיינו רבי יהושע, הואיל ובא להעיד על זאת יפה כוון ודקדק בדבר אל נכון:
Rashi on Chullin 7a:9:4.english: See what a great man testified about him - See what a great man testified about him, namely Rabbi Yehoshua, since he came to testify about this, he aimed and was precise about the matter correctly.

Tosafot on Chullin 7a:1:1.hebrew: אלא מקום הניחו לו אבותיו להתגדר בו - תימה דלא משני הכי בפרק במה בהמה (שבת דף נו:) דדרשינן ואת הבמות אשר על פני ירושלים אשר בנה שלמה (אותם בער יאשיהו) כו', אפשר בא אסא כו', אלא מקיש ראשונים לאחרונים, מה אחרונים לא עשו ותלה בהן, אף כו'; ואמאי לא משני דמקום הניחו לו אבותיו להתגדר בו כדמשני הכא? ויש לומר, דבשלמא הכא גבי נחש הנחושת, לפי שנעשה על פי הדבור, טעו בו הראשונים והיו סבורים שהיה אסור לבערו; אלא התם, במה היו טועין שלא לבער אותן הבמות:
Tosafot on Chullin 7a:1:1.english: Rather, it is a place his ancestors left for him to distinguish himself with - It is astonishing that [the Gemara] does not answer this way in Perek Bameh Behemah (Shabbat 56b), where we expound [the verse] "and the high places that were before Jerusalem, which Solomon built... (those did Josiah remove)," etc. - "Is it possible that Asa came [and did not remove them]," etc.? Rather, [Scripture] juxtaposes the earlier [kings] to the later ones: just as the later ones did not act [to remove them], and yet [Scripture] hung [praise] upon them, so too, etc. And why does [the Gemara] not answer there that "it was a place his ancestors left him to distinguish himself with," as it answers here? One can say: Here, regarding the copper serpent, since it was made by [Divine] command, the early [kings] erred about it and thought it was forbidden to destroy it; but there, in what would they have erred, that they did not destroy those high places?

Tosafot on Chullin 7a:9:1.hebrew: ודילמא נתן עיניו בצד זה ואכל בצד אחר - וא"ת: דתנן בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף לד.) ספק חשכה מעשרין את הדמאי, הא ודאי חשכה לא, אמאי? כיון דאפשר ע"י נותן עיניו בצד זה ואוכל בצד אחר, אם כן יהא מותר להפריש בשבת, כדמוכח בפרק נוטל (שבת דף קמא:) ד רבי יהודה אומר אף מעלין את המדומע באחד ומאה, ופריך בגמרא (שם דף קמב.) והא מתקן הוא, ומשני: הא מני? רבי שמעון בן אלעזר היא, דאמר נותן עיניו בצד זה ואוכל בצד אחר, ולהכי לא חשיב תקון בשבת כשמעלה. ויש לומר דשאני מדומע שכבר היה נתקן, אבל תחלתו של טבל לא שרי על ידי דאפשר ליתן עיניו בצד זה ולאכול בצד אחר. [וע"ע תוספות גיטין לא. ובמנחות נה. ובבכורות נט. ד"ה במחשבה]:
Tosafot on Chullin 7a:9:1.english: And perhaps he fixed his eyes on this side and ate from the other side - And if you ask: for we learned in Perek Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 34a): If it is doubtful whether it has become dark, one tithes demai (doubtfully-tithed produce); but if it is certainly dark, one may not — why? Since it is possible by fixing one's eyes on this side and eating from the other side, if so, it should be permitted to separate [tithes] on Shabbat, as is evident from Perek Notel (Shabbat 141b), that Rabbi Yehuda says: One may even raise up the medumma (produce mixed with untithed produce) with one [part] in a hundred. And the Gemara there raises a difficulty (ibid. 142a): But isn't this an act of rectifying? And it answers: Whose view is this? It is that of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, who says that one fixes his eyes on this side and eats from the other side, and therefore it is not considered rectifying on Shabbat when he raises it up. And one could say that medumma is different, since it had already been rectified; but the initial state of tevel is not permitted by means of the possibility of fixing one's eyes on this side and eating from the other side. [See also Tosafot on Gittin 31a, and on Menachot 55a, and on Bekhorot 59a, s.v. "bemachshava."]
